A.explanation: Resistors do not have e.m.f., they have potential difference. Also the battery p.d. is shared, not repeated across each resistor.

B.explanation: In series the e.m.f. $E$ is shared between the four resistors, so each resistor has only a fraction of $E$ as its potential difference.

C.explanation: The phrase e.m.f. across the resistors is wrong. E.m.f. describes energy supplied by the battery, while resistors have potential difference where energy is dissipated.

D.explanation: By conservation of energy the total energy per charge supplied, $E$, equals the total energy per charge dissipated, so the sum of the resistor potential differences equals $E$.

hints: Notice the diagram has one battery of e.m.f. $E$ in a single series loop with four resistors - identify which part supplies electrical energy and which parts convert it to heat.
Recall the definitions: e.m.f. is work done per charge by the source, while potential difference is work done per charge in a resistor. Only the battery can have e.m.f.
Connect energy conservation around the loop to the voltages: the energy per coulomb given out by the battery must equal the sum of the energies per coulomb lost in the series resistors.
walkthrough: Look at the circuit: a single loop with a battery of e.m.f. $E$ and negligible internal resistance in series with resistors. The same current flows through all components.

State the rule: e.m.f. $E = W/Q$ is energy per unit charge supplied by the source. Potential difference $V = W/Q$ across a resistor is energy per unit charge dissipated in that resistor. Resistors do not create e.m.f.
Because internal resistance is negligible, no energy is lost inside the battery, so the terminal potential difference across the battery equals its e.m.f. $E$.

Apply conservation of energy for one charge going once round the loop: energy supplied = sum of energies dissipated, so $E = V_1 + V_2 + V_3 + V_4$. This is Kirchhoff's second law for a series circuit.
This rejects the other wordings: each resistor has only part of $E$, and the word e.m.f. must not be used for a resistor. This is option D.
